one_liner: Hands-on mechanic repairing and maintaining U.S. Capitol Police fleet vehicles and installing police emergency equipment like lights, sirens and radios.
fit_summary: This is a skilled trades job requiring a year of hands-on automotive repair experience and current ASE certifications in five areas, none of which appear in your background. Your emergency-management consulting, policy knowledge and people skills don't substitute, and the posting says there is no education substitution. Only apply if you actually hold the ASE certifications and mechanic experience; otherwise target USCP or legislative-branch roles in administration, outreach or emergency preparedness.
eligibility: Open to the public; U.S. citizenship required, no federal status needed.
One year (52 weeks) of specialized automotive repair experience equivalent to CP-06/GS-08 (overhauling components, brake/engine/valve adjustments, diagnostics, HVAC servicing).

Current ASE certifications in all five areas (Suspension and Steering, Brakes, Electrical/Electronic Systems, Heating and Air Conditioning, Engine Performance), and copies must be attached or the application is incomplete.
No education substitution for experience at this grade.
Must pass a full field background investigation and a one-year probationary period.
strategy: Be honest first: if you lack ASE certifications in all five areas and a year of hands-on repair work, don't apply, because the questionnaire and documents will screen you out.

Instead, use this posting as a lead to watch USCP and other Legislative Branch openings in administration, community outreach, emergency preparedness or operations planning, where your IEM experience fits.
Frame your IEM work around concrete duties you actually did, such as preparedness planning, government client coordination and disaster recovery support, for those better-fit roles.
If you do have mechanic experience, list each job with dates, hours per week and specific repair tasks using the posting's terms, within the two-page USAJOBS limit.
Upload all five current ASE certificates and address the KSAs in narrative responses before the November 5, 2026 close.
resume_bullets: [Only if true] Diagnosed and repaired [vehicle types] brake, steering and suspension systems using [test equipment], completing [number] repairs per [week/month]; [hours] hrs/week, [dates].
[Only if true] Performed preventive maintenance and service inspections on a fleet of [number] vehicles, including installing [emergency lighting/radios/sirens].
[For better-fit roles] Coordinated [preparedness/recovery task] with [government client type] at IEM, supporting [specific program or deliverable]; [hours] hrs/week, [dates].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you diagnose an intermittent electrical fault on a fleet vehicle.
Describe your experience installing and troubleshooting emergency lights, sirens and radios.
How do you prioritize repairs when several mission-critical vehicles are down at once?
How do you check completed work for quality and safety?
watch_outs: ASE certifications in all five areas are mandatory and must be attached, a hard disqualifier without them.
On-site DC work with no telework, so expect a commute from Manassas.
Full field background investigation and one-year probation.
